claims.text: Rapid heating–quenching cycling induces microstructural heterogeneities in the HEA.
The induced heterogeneities accelerate protective oxide-film formation and reformation during tribocorrosion.
Faster passive-film reformation reduces the corrosion component of degradation despite intermittent mechanical removal of the film.
Duplex stainless steel lacks the rapid-cycling-induced microstructural features attributed to the treated HEA.
Duplex stainless steel re-establishes its passive oxide less efficiently than the thermally cycled HEA.
Rapid heating–quenching produces grain refinement in the HEA.
Rapid heating–quenching produces elemental segregation in the HEA.
Refined or compositionally heterogeneous regions act as nucleation sites for passive oxide formation.
Rapid regeneration of mechanically removed oxide limits exposure of the underlying HEA to the corrosive environment.
Slower film reformation in duplex stainless steel causes greater overall degradation than in the treated HEA.
The treated HEA will have lower total tribocorrosion degradation than duplex stainless steel under identical test conditions.
The treated HEA will have a lower corrosion rate than duplex stainless steel.
The treated HEA's wear component will be similar to or slightly greater than that of duplex stainless steel.
The wear component will not dominate total degradation because of rapid protective-film reformation.
The predicted advantage should hold when mechanical action removes the passive film intermittently without preventing its rapid reformation.
The mechanism may fail under extreme wear or in environments that suppress passive-film formation kinetics.
High temperatures or highly aggressive media may suppress the proposed passive-film mechanism.

Using identical test conditions for the treated HEA and conventionally processed duplex stainless steel ensures that observed differences are attributable to thermal-cycling-induced microstructural changes.
Failure of the HEA to show faster or more robust film reformation together with equal or greater overall or corrosion-specific degradation than duplex stainless steel would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions field claims that identical testing makes differences attributable to thermal-cycling-induced microstructure, but the comparison changes both alloy identity and treatment: a cycled HEA is compared with conventionally processed duplex stainless steel. Composition, phase constitution, hardness, and native passivation behavior therefore remain confounded, so this baseline cannot isolate the effect of thermal cycling.
